label: C-802 launcher canisters on PNS Zulfiquar (gallery context)

note: CHANGED from same_family to context. The units are the missile (ammunition) itself, and this picture shows only sealed launcher boxes on a Pakistani ship, so nothing of the missile's shape can be seen. That makes it unfit as the unit's picture. Keep it as gallery context only. Ids are correct: both are YJ-82 records. Licence CC BY-SA 4.0 with no problem shown.

label: Emad missile launch (gallery context)
what_it_shows: Real photo of an Emad ballistic missile just after lift-off in a large exhaust cloud. No launcher, TEL or vehicle can be seen. A tiny figure stands at the lower left.
note: CHANGED from same_family to context. wp_emad_tel is the TEL land unit, and the picture shows only the missile in flight with no vehicle, so it does not show the unit's own subject. Use it in the gallery only. Tasnim CC BY 4.0 is acceptable, and no watermark is visible.

label: Fattah unveiling ceremony

note: Rejection upheld. The main subject is a person, the missile is cropped and obscured, the backdrop is CGI, and there is no TEL (unit wp_fattah1_tel). The metadata image filename is truncated ('...unveiling_class.jpg'), but it is the right file.

label: Hedgehog ASW mortar on HMS Westcott, WWII (class photo)
what_it_shows: Black-and-white WWII photo of a Hedgehog spigot-mortar mounting on a destroyer's forecastle. Several projectiles are loaded on the spigots and clearly visible.
note: No change. The unit is the Hedgehog projectile, used in the Thai and Philippine packs, and the projectiles are visible on a Royal Navy mounting, so it is a class photo. IWM A-series, expired Crown Copyright (PD).

label: Igla-S display set, IDELF-2008
what_it_shows: Trade-fair booth. A grip-stock launcher tube on a table is stencilled '...-MAKET' (mock-up), a display missile sits on a stand above it, and an 'IGLA-SUPER' poster hangs behind.
note: Rejection upheld. The launcher is marked as a mock-up, which the owner rules exclude. It is also the Igla-S (9K338), not the 9K38 of wp_9k38_launcher. At most gallery context, if the owner chooses.

label: 3M-54E1 display model, MAKS-2009
what_it_shows: A glossy white 3M-54E1 missile model on stands on a display table. The Novator placard reads 'масштаб 1:10' (scale 1:10), and part of a second model is visible.
note: Rejection upheld. The Commons description says 'Макет' (mock-up) and the placard gives a scale. It is a model, not real hardware.

label: Kh-35UE anti-ship missile at MAKS-2015 (class photo)
what_it_shows: Full-size air-launched Kh-35UE stencilled 'Х-35УЭ-001', with handling stencils ('НЕ ТРОГАТЬ', 'ОПОРА'), on stands at MAKS-2015. It is the clear main subject, with visitors and other missiles behind.
note: No change. The Kh-35UE is the modernised export version, so it is a class photo for su_kh-35 (the air-launched version in the MiG-29, Su-27 and UMW packs). The service stencils show real hardware or a full-scale article, not a scale model. The '© Vitaly V. Kuzmin' corner credit is the photographer's own and matches his CC BY-SA 4.0 Commons uploads, so it is not an agency watermark. The owner may want it cropped out.

label: Mk 48 ADCAP torpedo unloaded from USS Annapolis (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real USN photo of a green Mk 48 ADCAP torpedo slung from a crane above the snow-covered USS Annapolis (SSN 760) at Groton, with sailors and loading gear.
note: No change. The torpedo is fairly small but recognisable. The mod cannot be identified, so it is a class photo for all eight Mk 48 ids, which are all Mk 48 torpedoes. USN photo, public domain.

label: R.550 Magic 2 on a French Air Force Mirage 2000C, 1999 (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real air-to-air photo looking under a Mirage 2000 wing. A Super 530D with a white radome fills the foreground. A Magic on the outer pylon sits at upper right, with its glass seeker dome, canards and tail fins clearly visible.
note: Second review: no change. It is a genuine photograph and the Magic is clearly identifiable, but it is the secondary subject. Magic 1 and Magic 2 cannot be told apart externally, so it stays a class photo. The description reads 'Super 350', a typo for Super 530. USAF PD, no watermark.

label: RIM-161 SM-3 launch from a US Navy Aegis warship (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real photo of a Standard missile with a booster climbing from a VLS through a large orange exhaust cloud. A 5-inch gun mount is in the foreground and an Aegis ship's superstructure and lattice mast are behind it.
note: Second review: changed the label and description. The Commons description says only 'SM-3 launch'. It does not name the ship, and from this angle the ship could be a Ticonderoga or a Burke, so the 'Arleigh Burke-class' and 'aft VLS' claims were removed. SM-2 and SM-3 look much alike at this distance, so the SM-3 identity rests on the file description. The block cannot be identified, so it stays a class photo for all three ids. USN PD.

label: RUM-139 VL-ASROC launch from USS Mustin (DDG-89), 2014 (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real photo of a VL-ASROC rising out of the forward VLS of an Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, beside the Mk 45 5-inch/62 gun, with the SPY-1 array and bridge behind it. The missile is clearly visible.
note: Second review: no change. The ids are the same weapon in two mods (hyphen and underscore spellings). The variant cannot be told apart, so it is a class photo. USN PD.

label: S-125 Newa fire-control radar, Polish service, 2019 (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real photo at a 2019 Polish Navy open day. The SNR-125 Low Blow antenna group stands camouflaged on its mount. A wheeled truck-mounted launcher with two V-601 missiles is behind it, and visitors and soldiers are in the foreground.
note: Second review: no change. The radar is clearly the subject. wp_newa (the T-55-based tracked launcher in the mod) is still correctly excluded, because the launcher shown is wheeled. The description says Newa-SC, but the upgrade cannot be confirmed visually, so it stays a class photo. CC BY-SA 4.0. The people are incidental.

label: TARPS pod on an F-14 Tomcat aboard USS George Washington (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real deck photo. Ordnancemen in green jerseys use a loading cart to remove a grey TARPS pod marked 31 from under an F-14's belly. The pod fills most of the frame.
note: Second review: no change. Whether this is the late digital TARPS (CD/DI) cannot be seen, so it is a class photo. USN PD.

label: BGM-109 Tomahawk launched from USS Missouri (BB-63), Desert Storm 1991 (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real black-and-white photo of a Tomahawk climbing away on its booster past the battleship Missouri's forward superstructure, with its Phalanx mounts and fire-control directors. The missile is clear against the sky.
note: Second review: no change. Pre-Block IV Tomahawks (TASM, TLAM-C and Block III) look the same externally, so it is a class photo for the B/C ids. It is a surface launch, so for the UGM ids it is a class photo only. The Block IV/V ids (E/J/M) get the alt1 photo instead. USN PD.

label: Tactical Tomahawk Block IV in test flight, China Lake 2002 (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real air-to-air photo of a white Tactical Tomahawk Block IV test round over the sea, with NAVAIR and Raytheon markings, orange test fins and its wings deployed.
note: Second review: no change. It is a genuine photograph. It shows a prototype in test livery, not a service round, so it is a class photo for the Block IV ids and the Block V-derived ids (E5, J, M, which are modded). The Raytheon logo is a manufacturer marking, not a watermark. USN PD.

label: Beriev Be-12 Chayka '25 yellow', preserved (class photo)
what_it_shows: Real photo of a preserved light-grey Be-12 amphibian, side number 25 in yellow, on grass at an outdoor aircraft museum, with a MiG and an airliner behind it. It shows the gull wing, the AI-20 turboprops, the glazed navigator's nose and the radome.
note: Second review: no change. Be-12 and Be-12N look the same externally, so it is a class photo for both. The museum is not verified, so the caption does not name it. Not usable for the Vietnamese operator. CC BY-SA 2.0.

label: Beriev Be-12 (Ukrainian Navy, 2014; class photo)
what_it_shows: Sharp air-to-air side view of a grey Be-12 amphibian in flight against a blue sky. It wears yellow side number 02, a Ukrainian trident on the fin and the Ukrainian naval ensign on the nose.
note: Second review: no change. It is a real photo of the right type. The operator is post-Soviet Ukraine, not the Soviet AV-MF, so same_family is correct. Be-12 and Be-12N are externally near-identical, so both ids are fine. The image is a US Navy public-domain photo with no watermark.

label: Giraffe AMB radar on MAN HX77 (British Army, Farnborough 2018; class photo)
what_it_shows: A Giraffe AMB with its mast raised, on a green MAN HX 8x8 truck. The truck has UK plate PT 97 AB and a Union flag, and a Saab 'Giraffe AMB' placard stands in front. Airshow setting.
note: Second review: no change. It is the same radar and matches the HX77 carrier in the mod's text, but the operator is British, not Swedish, so same_family is right. This is the best main-picture candidate of the three.

label: Giraffe AMB radar, containerised version (class photo)
what_it_shows: A tan containerised Giraffe AMB standing on jack legs, its mast raised and wrapped in camouflage netting. A second unit is partly visible on the right, and pine trees and a sports field are in the background.
note: Second review: no change. It is a real photo of the same radar, but with no truck carrier, which differs from the mod, and the operator is unknown. Gallery use only; same_family stays.

label: Giraffe AMB radar (French Air Force, Renault truck; class photo)
what_it_shows: A green Giraffe AMB shelter on a Renault Kerax truck with its mast raised and a 'French Air Force Giraffe AMB' placard. A white Skeldar UAV display airframe sits in the foreground.
note: Second review: no change. The radar is the clear main subject, and the Skeldar display item is incidental foreground, not a mock-up of the subject. The operator is French and the carrier differs, so it stays same_family.

label: Mil Mi-26 (Russian Air Force, Zhukovsky 2012; class photo)
what_it_shows: Full side view of a dark grey Mi-26 on static display, marked VVS ROSSII with a red star, side number 88 and an RF- registration.

label: Mil Mi-6 (CCCP-11325, civil markings; class photo)

note: Second review: no change to the verdict. It is a real photo and clearly an Mi-6 with wings and tanks. The civil CCCP registration and early era differ from the mod's grey military Mi-6A, so it is same_family. Quality is poor but usable, so owner_check stays: prefer a better military Mi-6A photo if one turns up.

label: WZ-10 UAV (PLAAF, Changchun Air Force Open Day 2025)

note: Second review: I agree with upgrading this to same_type against the audit's class_photo. The PLAAF placard and insignia identify the PLA WZ-10 itself, not an export WL-10 demonstrator. owner_check stays true because this overrides the audit.

label: Andrea Doria-class cruiser Caio Duilio (C 554), Taranto 1985 (class photo)

note: Second review: no change. Only the Andrea Doria-class id is assigned; no Vittorio Veneto, Audace, Alpino or Sparviero ids, because those ships are not shown, and the background ships cannot be identified. The 1985 training configuration means it stays same_family.

what_it_shows: A sharp colour photo of the F125 frigate Baden-Württemberg, with F222 on the bow, underway in harbour at Wilhelmshaven. It is not a Brandenburg (F123) or Sachsen (F124) class ship.

No change from the first review.

label: Galicia-class LPD at Rota

The framing is mediocre because the breakwater cuts off half the ship, so the owner may prefer a better picture. CC BY 2.0.

label: Soviet Don-class submarine tender (963), 1970

note: Kept. This is a real photo of the right boat type: a USCG training boat built to mimic a smuggling go-fast, not an actual smuggler. It is labelled as a type photo. The helicopter is prominent but does not hide the boat. USCG public domain.

note: Kept as a class photo. The 2009 date fits the post-upgrade ship, which is close to exact for ran_ffg_adelaide_late, but the photo is bow-on and the upgrade fit cannot be seen. Ballarat dominates the frame, so the picture needs a crop or a careful caption. USN public domain.

label: HMS Amazon (F169), Type 21 frigate, 1986

note: CHANGED from same_type to same_family. The ship is a named variant and the photo is in era, but the unit's ACSL/Lynx fit is not visibly confirmed. The first reviewer's claim that a helicopter is visible aft does not hold up. The kit audit also rated it a class photo. The owner may upgrade it to same_type. USN public domain.

label: HMS Leander (F109) at Devonport, 1977
what_it_shows: A soft, grainy and colour-shifted slide scan of an Ikara-conversion Leander frigate moored alongside the depot ship HMS Defiance at Devonport. The pennant is barely legible and fine detail is lost.
note: Kept as context, for the gallery only. The subject and era are right for rn_ff_leander_batch1, but the quality is too poor for an encyclopedia picture. It is borderline even as gallery material, so the owner may reject it. The other Leander ids are correctly excluded. CC BY-SA 2.0.

label: Rothesay-class frigate HMS Rothesay (F107), 1987
what_it_shows: Real black-and-white aerial photo. HMS Rothesay is broadside with pennant F107 clearly legible and shows her 1980s modernised fit: Lynx hangar and Seacat aft, twin 4.5in forward. A surfaced Whiskey-class submarine is in the foreground.
note: Second review: confirmed as a real photo of the exact ship. F107 is Variant2 of rn_ff_rothesay. I corrected the first reviewer's 'post-Ikara-conversion' wording: Rothesays received a Seacat/Lynx refit, not Ikara. same_type applies to rn_ff_rothesay only. For rnzn_ff_rothesay (Otago/Taranaki) it must be labelled 'Class photo' (same_family): different operator and fit. USN PD.

label: Unidentified frigate refuelling from USS Hornet, 1967
what_it_shows: Taken from Hornet's deck: a 5in/38 mount and its crew dominate the frame. Part of a frigate's hull and superstructure is alongside, cropped and partly hidden.
note: Second review: I agree with the rejection. The Commons description admits the ship may be an RAN River-class DE, and the subject is obscured and cropped.

label: Kara-class (Project 1134B) cruiser, pennant 539 (Class photo)
what_it_shows: Real colour photo of a Kara-class cruiser at speed, bow quarter, pennant 539. The Top Sail and Head Net radars, twin Storm/Head Lights directors, the SS-N-14 tubes and the bow anchor gear are all clear.
note: Second review: unchanged. This is a Cold War Kara in the original fit, and nothing identifies it as Kerch. It is only a labelled 'Class photo' for the late (L) unit. DoD PD.

label: Kara-class cruiser Petropavlovsk moored in port, 1992 (Class photo)
what_it_shows: Real backlit photo of a Kara-class cruiser moored bow-on alongside other warships. The Top Sail mast, the twin Head Lights directors and the funnel are recognisable as a Kara. The hull is mostly in silhouette.
note: Second review: unchanged. Petropavlovsk is a sister of Kerch, and the photo is poorly lit. Use it as a gallery fallback 'Class photo' only, not the main picture.

label: Slava-class cruiser Marshal Ustinov (055), post-modernisation
what_it_shows: Sharp, real aerial colour photo from an RN Merlin of a Slava-class cruiser, pennant 055, with her name in Cyrillic on the stern. She is in the post-refit fit, with a new planar radar on the foremast and the P-1000 tubes, Top Dome and AK-130 visible.
note: Second review: confirmed. This is the exact ship and modernised fit for wp_rkr_slavaLU, so same_type applies to slavaLU only. For wp_rkr_slavaLV (Varyag) it must be labelled 'Class photo' (same_family): a sister ship in a different fit. OGL v1.0, credit LPHOT Seeley/MOD.

label: Slava-class cruiser Marshal Ustinov (070), 1994 (Class photo)
what_it_shows: Real aerial colour photo of a Slava-class cruiser at speed, pennant 070, in her original pre-refit fit with lattice Top Pair/Top Steer radars. Some film grain.
note: Second review: unchanged. This is pre-modernisation Ustinov, so it is only a labelled 'Class photo' for slavaLU (late radar fit) and slavaLV (Varyag). USN PD.

label: Ulsan-class frigate ROKS Kyongbuk (FF-956), RIMPAC 92
what_it_shows: Real colour aerial photo of an Ulsan-class frigate, pennant 956, off San Diego. Twin 76mm mounts, Harpoon canisters aft and the funnel/mast arrangement are clearly visible.
note: Second review: unchanged. Gyeongbuk FF-956 is a named variant of ko_ff-951. No other listed unit (Incheon, Daegu, Pohang, Chamsuri) is shown, so the tags are correct. USN PD.

note: Second review: confirmed that the ship is Incheon (FFG-811), and only ko_ffg-811 is tagged. The overlay is the source's own credit, not a press agency mark, and the licence is CC BY-SA 2.0. note: Second review: confirmed, no change. The language file lists Seoul FFG-821 as Variant3 of ko_ffg-818 (Daegu Class), so this is the unit's own ship. No other candidate applies; ko_ffg-828 Chungnam is a different class. USN public domain.

label: Type 037II missile boat Nanhai (772), Hong Kong garrison

note: Second review: confirmed. vessel_names.ini lists Nanhai PTG-772 as Variant3 of plan_ptg_type037IIE, so this is the unit's own boat even though the mod uses the '037IIE' designation. Owner check kept only for that caption question. Licence is CC BY 3.0 (attribution: Tksteven).

label: Type 052C destroyer Lanzhou (170)
what_it_shows: Real colour photograph of Type 052C destroyer 170 (Lanzhou) underway with crew manning the rails and dressed flags. AESA panels are visible. It looks like a scan or reproduction of a print.
note: Second review: the subject is confirmed. vessel_names.ini lists Lanzhou DDG-170 as Variant1 of plan_ddg_type_052C_rsa. Licence concern remains: the image looks like a Chinese official or press photo that reached the CRS report through the Navy Office of Legislative Affairs, so the public-domain claim is doubtful. The owner should verify the licence before import.

label: Type 052D destroyer Jiaozuo (163)
what_it_shows: Sharp real photo of PLAN destroyer 163 Jiaozuo moored at St Petersburg, with Chinese, Russian and St Andrew's flags. The bow, the 130 mm gun, the forward VLS, the bridge, the fixed-array superstructure and the mast with its radome are all clear. A Russian warship is behind it.
note: Second review: no change. The photo is real and the subject is confirmed. Jiaozuo is a late-build 052D(L), so it cannot be the exact picture for any single phase, and the class-photo label for all six ids is correct.

label: Type 054 frigate Ma'anshan (525)
what_it_shows: Real photo of frigate 525 Ma'anshan alongside at the shipyard under large blue gantry cranes. The whole stealthy hull and superstructure, the mast with the radome and the bow with pennant 525 are visible.
note: Second review: no change. This is the right Type 054 (not 054A), photographed in the fitting-out era. It could arguably be same_type for the base and Phase 1 units, but because one verdict covers all four ids including the late and Phase 2 variants, it stays same_family. The image is only 939 px wide. Credit the CC BY 2.0 author mclarenshen.

label: Forpost UAV (pre-localisation) - class photo
what_it_shows: Real photo of a grey Forpost UAV, number 912 and marked 'статика', on static ground display at Innovation Day 2013. The twin-boom pusher layout, the large mushroom satcom antenna, the sensor turret and the remove-before-flight tags are visible.
note: Second review: no change to the verdict. The airframe is externally almost the same as the Forpost-R, but this is the pre-localisation version, so it is only a class photo. The audit says the gallery already uses a verified MAKS-2011 Forpost photo and an earlier review rejected a replacement, so this file is probably redundant and the owner should decide. The image file on disk is named ..._class_photo_ka.jpg, without the trailing underscore of the group name. Make sure the importer maps it correctly.

label: Kamov Ka-27PL Helix-A, Russian Navy (yellow 09)
what_it_shows: Sharp real in-flight photo of a Russian Navy Ka-27 (yellow 09, number 19205) with the St Andrew's flag and a red star. The coaxial rotors, the chin radome, the flotation-gear housings and the light-blue naval scheme are visible.
note: Second review: the verdict is kept. The airframe matches the ASW Ka-27PL and the Commons title says PL; nothing points to a PS rescue variant. The audit asked to reject this airliners.net import (AN1971578) unless the free licence is confirmed. The kit records CC BY-SA 3.0 by Igor Dvurekov, but the description is empty. The owner should confirm the permission or licence before import.

label: Tupolev Tu-214R RF-64514, Russian Air Force
what_it_shows: Real photo of the Tu-214R RF-64514 (VVS Rossii) on approach with its gear down against a dark sky. The forward and centre side-looking radar fairings and the dorsal fairings are visible.
note: Second review: no change. This is the exact type. The Commons title says RA-64514, but the aircraft wears RF-64514. It is the same airframe, so this is harmless. msdvd_tu-214r_F (RF) and msdvd_tu-214_AEW (RM) are different or notional variants, and correctly they are not assigned.

label: Dassault Etendard IVM, Marine nationale (60)
what_it_shows: Real photo of a preserved Etendard IVM, number 60, in MARINE markings with an anchor roundel, on the Intrepid museum flight deck in front of the Manhattan skyline. The tail of a tiger-striped jet and a MiG-21 (4105) are partly visible behind it.
note: Second review: no change. The type, the variant (IVM, as the fin plate shows) and the operator all match. It is a museum airframe, but the configuration is representative. No Mirage, Alizé or helicopter ids apply.

label: Breguet Br.1050 Alizé, Marine nationale (59, F-AZYI)
what_it_shows: Real panning photo of the airworthy Alizé 59 (F-AZYI) taxiing at AirExpo 2016 in late dark-grey Marine markings. The retracted radome, the wing nacelle pods and the canopy antenna are visible.
note: CHANGED from same_type to same_family. The mod has three French standards: the 1959 base, the ALM of 1979-83 and the ALH of 1996-97. Alizé 59 is a late-standard airframe preserved in its final scheme, and the photo cannot tell which standard it carries. One verdict covers all three ids, so the variant is in doubt and the image should be labelled as a class photo. in_br1050 (Indian Navy) is correctly not assigned.

label: Sud-Est Aquilon 203 (Sea Venom family), Lorient 1973
what_it_shows: Real 1973 colour slide of a preserved dark-blue Aquilon, coded 53, with folded wings, displayed on grass at Lorient. Another Aquilon marked 'AQUILON 203' is behind it.
note: Second review: no change. The Commons title says this is an Aquilon 203, not the unit's 202, so it is a class photo. The slide colour is dated but the subject is clear.

label: Eurocopter AS332 Super Puma, French Air Force (2233/FY)
what_it_shows: A real photo of a silver French Air Force AS332 Super Puma taxiing on an airfield with its rotors turning. Sharp front-quarter view.
note: Confirmed. This is a French Air Force transport airframe (L/L1 family), not the B, F or M variants, so it stays a class photo for the three AS332 ids only. It is not a Cougar, so the AS532 ids stay off. No change.

label: French military Cougar-family helicopter, Afghanistan
what_it_shows: A real photo of a grey French military Super Puma/Cougar-family helicopter flying low over troops in Afghanistan. It has a nose FLIR turret, large sponsons and a door gunner.
note: Kept as same_family with owner_check. The title says French Army Cougar, but the long sponsons and FLIR could also fit an EC725 Caracal. If it is a Caracal, it is only a family photo. The licence is listed as public domain with the author given as 'see source page'; confirm the source is US DoD. No change.

label: Airbus VSR700 rotary-wing drone (demonstrator, ILA Berlin)
what_it_shows: A real photo of a grey Airbus VSR700 drone with a Guimbal-based airframe and a sensor ball, sitting on a static display plinth at an air show. An H135 is behind it, and the crowd's faces are blurred.
note: CHANGED from same_type to same_family. It is the Airbus demonstrator in company livery on a show plinth, not a French Navy airframe, and it may be a full-scale display example rather than a flying airframe. Use it as a class photo until the owner confirms it is real hardware.

label: Dassault Mirage IIIE, Armée de l'Air (EC 2/4, 1986)
what_it_shows: A real black-and-white photo of a camouflaged French Mirage IIIE, code 4-BE, parked with drop tanks in front of a hangar shelter. Clear front-quarter view.
note: Confirmed. The units in the mapping are fr_mirage_iii (RADF, Australian), Mirage_III (Royal Navy mod, Argentine), paf_mirage_iii (Pakistani) and spa_mirage_iii (Spanish Mirage IIIEE). None is French, so this is a class photo for all four. USAF, public domain. No change.

label: Eurocopter AS350 B3 Ecureuil (Wucher Helicopter, Austria)
what_it_shows: A real photo of a civilian AS350 B3 Ecureuil, OE-XHO, in Wucher livery, flying against an overcast sky. Sharp.
note: Confirmed as a class photo. It is a B3, while the units are the AS.350B (civil) and the RAN AS.350BA trainer and recon. No change.

label: Submarine Galerna (S-71), Málaga
what_it_shows: A real photo, a scanned colour print, of an Agosta-class submarine surfaced and berthing in Málaga harbour, with crew handling lines. The hull and sail are clear.
note: Confirmed as a class photo. The photo is undated, so it cannot be tied to the Early or Late fit, and the pennant number cannot be read on the sail; the identity as S-71 rests on the file title. Hashmat is a Pakistani Agosta, so it is a class photo for that unit too. No change.

label: IAF F-16C Barak 2020 (557), Tel Nof 2017
what_it_shows: A real photo of an Israeli Air Force F-16C, tail 557, in desert camouflage with a squadron emblem, on static display with tanks and AAMs. A second F-16 is partly visible behind it.
note: Confirmed as same_family. 'Barak 2020' is not proven to be the same as the mod's 'Barak II'. It shows only the F-16, so only the F-16 id is assigned. No change.

label: Swedish Air Force JAS 39 Gripen (179), Bulgaria 2003
what_it_shows: A real photo of a single-seat Swedish JAS 39 Gripen, tail 179, rolling on a runway with a centreline tank. Sharp side view.
note: Confirmed as same_family. It is a 2003 airframe, probably an A model with no refuelling probe visible, while the mod's weapons suggest the C/D standard. USAF, public domain. No change.

label: Philippine Air Force FA-50PH, Exercise Pitch Black 2026
what_it_shows: A real night photograph of a grey FA-50PH on a floodlit ramp, with two PAF ground crew doing pre-flight checks. The tandem canopy, nose, intake, centreline and wing tanks, and gear are clear. The tail is cut off at the upper left. F-16s are parked in the background.
note: Second review: unchanged. The type and operator match FA-50PH. The F-16s in the background are small and out of focus and do not count as depicting iaf_f-16c-barakII, and no Gripen is visible. Owner check stays on. The file is dated 2026 and is credited to the PAF as public domain, so an owner should confirm that PAF releases really are public domain, as the audit raised. The night lighting and the cropped tail make it a weaker lead image, but it is usable.

label: JGSDF V-22 Osprey JG-1706 at Camp Kengun, Resolute Dragon 2023
what_it_shows: A real photograph of two Ospreys on a ramp. The dominant one in the foreground is JGSDF V-22 JG-1706 / 91706, with 陸上自衛隊 markings. A USMC MV-22B ('01') sits behind it to the right, smaller in frame.
note: CHANGED: I removed mv22b_osprey. With only one verdict per image, keeping it at same_type would let this become the USMC unit's main picture. The repo gap note lists the JGSDF V-22 as the wrong subject for that unit and asks for a clean VMM-263/162 photo. The USMC aircraft is only secondary here. The photo is still an exact picture for jgsdf_mv22b_osprey. If the owner wants it as a gallery or class photo for mv22b_osprey, add that by hand.

label: Kilo 877V submarine B-871 Alrosa, Sevastopol
what_it_shows: A clear real photograph of a surfaced Kilo-class submarine, side-on in Sevastopol bay. The sail is clearly lettered 'АЛРОСА'.
note: Second review: unchanged. The name on the sail identifies the boat as B-871 Alrosa, the only 877V, and the description matches. The pump-jet stern is underwater, but the name is enough. Same_type stands.

label: Oberon-class submarine HMAS Onslow (RIMPAC 1998), class photo
what_it_shows: A real high-angle aerial photograph of an Oberon-class submarine running on the surface with masts raised. The full hull and sail are visible. The hull number cannot be read, so the identification as Onslow rests on the description.
note: Second review: unchanged. This is Onslow in 1998, late in service and after the SUBICS refit, so it is a class photo for the RAN-early unit. For rn_oberon_class it is a class photo because the operator is different.

label: Oscar-class SSGN (class photo)
what_it_shows: A real high-angle photograph of the bow and sail of a surfaced Oscar-class SSGN. It shows the very broad hull, the missile-hatch outlines and the anechoic tiles. The grain and colour look like a scanned film print. It is not artwork.
note: Second review: unchanged. It is a genuine photograph, but the frame does not show the hull length or the stern, so I cannot confirm Oscar I or Oscar II. It stays a class photo. The author field says '(see source page)'. The PD status is accepted as the kit checked it.

label: Gyrodyne QH-50C DASH on USS Nicholas, 1965 (class photo)
what_it_shows: A real black-and-white photograph of a QH-50C drone helicopter, with a 'NAVY QH-50C' tail plate, hovering over a destroyer's flight deck. The DASH controller stands in his booth.
note: Second review: unchanged. The variant is QH-50C, not QH-50E, and not the fictional armed QH-50D Pirate fit, so it is a class photo for both units.

label: Spanish Navy AV-8B+ Harrier II aboard USS Wasp, BALTOPS 2024
what_it_shows: A clear real photograph of a Spanish Navy Harrier II with ARMADA markings and Spanish roundels, taxiing on the deck of a US amphibious ship while a director signals. It has the enlarged radar nose of the Plus version and carries wing tanks.
note: CHANGED: I removed spa_av-8b and mm_av-8b_plus. With only one verdict per image, keeping them at same_type would wrongly pin a radar-nosed Spanish aircraft as the picture for the non-radar AV-8B and for the Italian operator. For those two units it is at most a class photo, which the owner can add by hand. It stays an exact picture for spa_av-8b_plus. It does not show the EF-18 or the Mirage F1.

label: Spanish Air Force EF-18 Hornets in formation, Aviano 2004 (class photo)
what_it_shows: A real photograph of four F/A-18 Hornets flying overhead in formation, seen from below as near-silhouettes against a pale sky. You can make out the planform, tanks and stores, but no markings can be read.
note: Second review: unchanged. The aircraft are identified as Spanish only by the description, and in 2004 they could have been EF-18A or EF-18M. They are silhouettes with no visible detail, so this is weak and is a class or gallery photo only. It does not show the Harrier or the Mirage F1. A borderline-quality call, so the owner should look.

label: Dassault Mirage F1M, Spanish Air Force (C.14-41 / 14-22, Ala 14, Tiger Meet 2011)
what_it_shows: A real photo of a single-seat Spanish Air Force Mirage F1 (C.14-41, code 14-22) taxiing, with a grey tiger-art tail and a striped centreline tank. The whole aircraft is sharp and in frame.
note: Second review: no change. This is a 2011 F1M upgrade, while the mod models the Cold War F1CE and F1EE (Spanish Navy Mod, Cold War), so it can only be a class photo for both. It shows no Harrier or EF-18, so those ids stay out. The small '© Flox Papa' mark is the author's own signature, not an agency watermark.

label: Yuan-class (Type 039A/041) submarine sail, Zhoushan 2011 (class photo)
what_it_shows: A real photo looking up at the sail of a PLAN Yuan-class submarine, dressed with flags, from the gangway during Adm. Mullen's July 2011 visit to Zhoushan. Two officers stand at left.
note: Second review: no change. The sail profile and the description both say Yuan, so it gets no plan_ss_type_039 (Song) id. The 039A or 039B sub-variant cannot be told from the sail alone, so it stays a class photo. The existing yuan_family asset is a different Mullen frame (him departing), so this is probably not a duplicate. The owner should still check it before adding a second Mullen-visit shot.

label: Type 212A submarine on the shiplift quay, HDW Kiel (class photo)
what_it_shows: A real photo of a complete Type 212 hull, unfinished or in refit, on the HDW Kiel shiplift with a mobile crane beside it and a Maersk ship behind. The full side profile with the X-rudder is visible.
note: Second review: no change. No hull number is visible, and the boat could be German or an Italian Todaro. The batch and upgrade state are unknown, so it stays a class photo for both units.

label: Whiskey-class (Project 613) submarine, Soviet Navy, c.1964 (class photo)
what_it_shows: A black-and-white aerial photo of a surfaced Soviet Whiskey-class submarine with sail number 026 running in the Pacific, with ships on the horizon.
note: Second review: no change. The operator differs, since the unit is the TNI-AL Whiskey, so it is a labelled class photo. The boat is small in the frame but its profile is identifiable.

label: 9M317 missile on a Buk-M2E launcher, MAKS 2007 (family context)
what_it_shows: A real photo, taken from below against blue sky, of a green 9M317 round on the launcher rail of a Buk-M2E at MAKS 2007. The stencil reads 'габаритно-массовый макет' (size-and-weight dummy).
note: Second review: no change. This is the rail-launched 9M317, not the container-launched 9M317M, so it is context only. The dummy is a real display round photographed on real hardware, not a scale model.

label: C-802 launcher canisters aboard PNS Zulfiquar (family context)
what_it_shows: A real photo of two quad C-802 canister launchers on the Pakistani F-22P frigate Zulfiquar, with the ship's nameboard in view. Only the closed canisters show; no missile is visible.
note: Second review: no change. These are ship-launched C-802 canisters, while the unit is the air-launched CM-802AKG, so the picture is gallery context only. Its value is weak.

label: Flight line at FOB Shank, Afghanistan, 2012 (context)
what_it_shows: A real photo of two MQ-1C Grey Eagle UAVs on the concrete apron at FOB Shank. Tent hangars, containers, light and antenna masts and an aerostat stand behind them.
note: Second review: no change. The base shows only as background, so the context value is weak, and FOB already has a same_type gallery photo, though that one has no credit. The owner may want to skip this one.

label: Shahed-136 drone at the IRGC exhibition, Qom 2023 (context)
what_it_shows: A real front-view photo of a Shahed-136 loitering munition on a display trolley. Exhibition boards with line drawings and a map stand behind it.
note: Second review: no change. The picture shows the drone itself, not the launcher (TEL) the units represent, so it is context only. The author is Tasnim News Agency, a state-linked press agency, but the file is CC BY 4.0 with no watermark; credit Tasnim. The owner should confirm they are happy to use Tasnim material.

label: M247 Sergeant York (cutaway drawing)
what_it_shows: Black-and-white line-art cutaway drawing of the M247 DIVAD turret and hull on an M48 chassis, with crew figures drawn in. It is not a photograph.
note: Second review: no change. It is a drawing, so the real-photos-only rule rejects it. usa_spaa_m247 still needs a real photo.

label: NAS Keflavik, Iceland, 1982 (aerial view)
what_it_shows: Real colour aerial photo of the NAS Keflavik ramp in 1982: runway, hangars, P-3 Orions, E-3 and C-141 type jets, a radome, a red and white water tower, and Keflavik/Njardvik town and the sea behind.
note: Second review: no change. It is a real photo, but it shows Keflavik and not Reykjavik airfield, so it is context only and the caption must name Keflavik. USAF public-domain photo, no licence problem seen.

label: Khawr Al Amaya oil terminal (KAAOT), Iraq, 2008
what_it_shows: Real photo at dawn of an offshore oil loading terminal: platforms on jackets linked by walkways, jack-up legs, loading arms and lights.
note: Second review: no change. The unit is a fictional armed Iranian rig with a helicopter. This is an Iraqi terminal with no visible helideck or weapons, so it is context only and the caption must name KAAOT. USN public-domain photo.

label: S-350E Vityaz 50P6E launcher, MAKS-2013
what_it_shows: Real photo of a BAZ 8x8 launcher with a 12-canister rack with red caps. The placard reads 'ПУ 50П6Е ЗРС С-350Е' (50P6E launcher, S-350E system). The edge of a second Vityaz vehicle shows at left.
note: Second review: no change. The placard confirms the 50P6E launcher, so ru_50n6 (the radar) is correctly left out. This is an export (E) prototype at an air show, not a Russian service vehicle, and the mod splits the TEL into LR/MR/SR loads that cannot be told apart here. So it stays 'Class photo' (same_family) for all three TEL ids. CC BY-SA 4.0 (Kuzmin), no problem seen.

label: Vertical-launch Sea Wolf (GWS26) firing from HMS Portland
what_it_shows: Real photo looking down on the 32-cell forward VLS silo of Type 23 frigate HMS Portland as a Sea Wolf missile leaves a cell, with the launch flame, open hatches, flying debris and Harpoon canisters in the foreground.
note: Second review: no change. A vertical launch from a Type 23 silo is GWS26, so this is the right subject and variant for both Euromod rows (Chile's ex-RN Type 23s are also GWS26). OGL Defence Imagery, no problem seen.

label: Finnish MTO-85M (RBS 15) coastal launcher on Sisu SK242, Helsinki 2017
what_it_shows: Real photo of a Finnish Sisu 8x8 truck carrying closed RBS 15 launcher boxes in a Helsinki parade, with crowds at the roadside.
note: Second review: no change. It is a real photo of the truck-borne RBS 15 coastal launcher family, but it is the Finnish operator on a Sisu truck, while the Swedish RBS 15 KA uses Volvo trucks. The boxes are closed and the variant cannot be told. Kept as 'Class photo' (same_family), not same_type. The owner may prefer context, as the audit said.

label: RBS 15 Mk3 mock-up at a trade show
what_it_shows: Indoor trade-show stand: a grey 'RBS 15' Mk3 missile mock-up on a plinth with a sales placard, in front of a cropped and partly hidden camouflaged launcher truck.
note: Second review: no change. The Commons description itself says 'mock-up', and the mock-up is the main subject. The real truck is cropped and blocked, so it cannot stand in as the unit picture.

label: Wing Loong II, Dubai Airshow 2017
what_it_shows: Real photo of a full-size Wing Loong II airframe (marked '翼龙II WING LOONG II') on static display, with LS-6, FT-9 and other weapons laid out in front. A Wing Loong I is at right. It is a photo, not a side-view drawing.
note: Second review: no change. The mod names the unit 'Wing Loong II, YL-2' under a PLAAF prefix. This is an AVIC export demonstrator, not a PLA service airframe, so it stays 'Class photo' (same_family). The weapons on the ground may be display rounds, but the airframe is real. CC BY-SA 4.0, no problem seen.

label: Wing Loong I UAV at MAKS-2017
what_it_shows: A real photo of a grey static-display MALE UAV at MAKS-2017, carrying a BA-7 missile on an underwing pylon and an EO turret under the nose. The fuselage is clearly lettered '翼龙 I / WING LOONG I'. There is a '© Vitaly V. Kuzmin' credit in the bottom-left corner.
note: Rejection confirmed. The airframe is the Wing Loong I, so the Commons title and description calling it a Wing Loong II are wrong, and it is not the subject of plaaf_yl-2. It is a different and smaller type, so it does not qualify as same_family either. The corner credit is the author's own attribution on a CC BY-SA file and is not a licence problem. No change from the first review.

label: Kirov-class cruiser Kalinin (085, later Admiral Nakhimov), 1991 — Class photo
what_it_shows: A real USN aerial colour photo of a Kirov-class nuclear cruiser with pennant 085, seen from the starboard bow. It is in the original Soviet fit: the red-deck P-700 hatch field forward, the original mast and radar domes, and the Soviet ensign.
note: Approval upheld as same_family only. It is the same hull (Kalinin was later renamed Admiral Nakhimov) in its 1991 configuration, not the 2025 refit with UKSK/Redut and the new mast, so it can never be same_type. The Commons licence is USN public domain, which is consistent with a DoD photo. The audit wanted context only; the owner should choose between 'Class photo' and gallery-only. No change from the first review.

label: USS Shiloh (CG-67) fires a Tomahawk, Operation Desert Strike, 1996
what_it_shows: A real USN photo of the forward two-thirds of a Ticonderoga-class cruiser with hull number 67 on the bow. It shows the SPY-1 deckhouse face, the forward Mk45 5in gun, the foremast and the forward funnel, with a Tomahawk climbing out of the forward Mk41 VLS. The stern and aft section are cropped out.
note: CHANGED from same_type to same_family. The ship is identifiable (CG-67 Shiloh, a VLS Ticonderoga), which refutes the audit's 'unidentified hull' claim, so the subject is right and both unit ids belong to it. However, the single verdict has to cover both units. For the 2025 unit this is a 1996 fit of a ship decommissioned in 2023, so it is a class photo, not the exact variant. It is also a cropped action shot rather than a full-ship view. For usn_cg_ticonderogaVLS_early (1994) it is a close era match, and the owner could promote it to that unit's own picture.

label: Open Mk41 VLS hatches aboard USS Hue City (CG-66)
what_it_shows: A real photo of a USN sailor inspecting open Mk41 VLS cell hatches during a yard period at Mayport, with barracks barge YRBM-L-27 behind. The ship itself is not visible.
note: Context upheld: it shows the launcher detail only and is for the gallery, never the unit picture. Public domain USN photo. No change from the first review.
